title: Add PHPUnit test coverage for critical plugin functions
description:
**Issue**: No automated tests exist for this plugin. Critical areas that need testing:
- validate_contact_value() in Items_Manager (security-critical)
- should_load_on_current_page() in Data Service
- sanitize_options() in Settings
- AJAX handlers (save/delete/reorder items)
- Frontend rendering logic

**Recommended approach**:
1. Add PHPUnit for PHP testing:
   - Create tests/ directory structure
   - Add phpunit.xml.dist
   - Test Items_Manager CRUD operations
   - Test Settings sanitization
   - Test Frontend conditional loading

2. Add Jest for JavaScript testing:
   - Test form validation in admin.js
   - Test platform URL generation
   - Test modal handling

**Files to create**:
- tests/bootstrap.php
- tests/phpunit.xml.dist
- tests/test-items-manager.php
- tests/test-settings.php
- tests/js/admin.test.js

**Estimated time**: 4-6 hours
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/ directory with PHPUnit setup
- phpunit.xml.dist configured
- Tests for validate_contact_value() with valid/invalid inputs
- Tests for sanitize_item_data() 
- Tests for Settings sanitization
- All tests pass: vendor/bin/phpunit

title: Remove legacy dead code from Frontend class
description:
**Issue**: After the Data Service refactor, several methods in class-frontend.php are now legacy/dead code:
- render_template() (lines 185-223) - replaced by render_template_optimized()
- render_fallback_template() (lines 259-317) - still used but duplicates logic from Data Service
- is_current_page_excluded() (lines 325-338) - logic moved to Data Service
- generate_platform_url() (lines 348-384) - duplicated, see separate issue
- get_platform_icon_url() (lines 393-395) - simple wrapper, keep or inline
- get_main_icon_url() (lines 403-416) - duplicated in Data Service

**Fix**:
1. Remove unused render_template() method
2. Update render_fallback_template() to use Data Service processed data
3. Remove is_current_page_excluded() as it's handled by Data Service
4. Consolidate URL/icon methods per duplication issue

**Files**: includes/class-frontend.php

**Estimated time**: 30 minutes
acceptance_criteria:
- render_template() method removed
- is_current_page_excluded() method removed
- generate_platform_url() removed (uses Items_Manager)
- get_main_icon_url() removed (uses Settings)
- Frontend still renders correctly via shortcode and auto-inject
close_reason: Removed legacy dead code: render_template() and is_current_page_excluded() methods

title: Remove redundant basename check in uninstall.php
acceptance_criteria:
- plugin_basename check removed (lines 22-24)
- WP_UNINSTALL_PLUGIN check remains as sole guard
- Uninstall works regardless of plugin folder name

title: Fix audit log: disable autoload and add 30-day rotation
acceptance_criteria:
- update_option() uses autoload=false for audit log
- Entries older than 30 days are filtered out before save
- Log still records new entries correctly
- Option not loaded on every page load (verify with Query Monitor)

title: Remove debug console.log from production admin.js
acceptance_criteria:
- console.log('QR code preview error:') removed
- No console.log statements in production code
- QR code error handling still works (silent fail or user notification)
close_reason: Removed debug console.log statement from production code

title: Upgrade deprecated npm dependencies (ESLint 9, remove rimraf)
description:
**Issue**: Several npm dependencies are deprecated or outdated:
- ESLint 8.57.0 - v8.x is deprecated, upgrade to v9.x
- glob (transitive) - deprecated, use native fs.glob or fast-glob
- rimraf 5.x - deprecated, use native fs.rm

**Current versions in package.json**:
\`\`\`json
"eslint": "^8.57.0"
"rimraf": "^5.0.7"
\`\`\`

**Fix**:
1. Upgrade ESLint to v9.x (requires config migration to flat config)
2. Replace rimraf with native Node.js fs.rm in package.json scripts:
   \`"clean": "node -e \"require('fs').rmSync('assets/css', {recursive:true, force:true}); require('fs').rmSync('assets/js', {recursive:true, force:true})\""\`
3. Run \`pnpm update\` to get latest compatible versions

**Files**: package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml

**Estimated time**: 1 hour (ESLint config migration takes time)
acceptance_criteria:
- ESLint upgraded to v9.x with flat config (eslint.config.js)
- rimraf removed, clean script uses native fs.rm
- pnpm build runs without errors
- pnpm lint runs without errors

title: Fix XSS vulnerability in admin.js jQuery .html() calls
acceptance_criteria:
- All jQuery .html() calls with dynamic content replaced with .text() or DOM methods
- No template literals directly inserted into DOM without escaping
- Tested: admin panel still functions correctly after changes
- No console errors in browser DevTools
close_reason: Fixed XSS vulnerabilities in showFieldError(), showFormError(), and showNotice() by replacing .html() template literals with safe DOM construction using .text()

title: Consolidate generate_platform_url() into Items_Manager
description:
**Issue**: generate_platform_url() is duplicated in 3 files with slight inconsistencies:
- includes/class-data-service.php (lines 247-282)
- includes/class-frontend.php (lines 348-384)
- includes/class-assets.php (lines 303-339)

**Inconsistency**: Zalo URL differs:
- Data Service: 'https://zalo.me/' . \$contact_value . '?openChat=true'
- Frontend/Assets: 'https://zalo.me/' . \$contact_value (missing ?openChat=true)

Also duplicated: get_main_icon_url() in Data Service and Frontend.

**Fix**: 
1. Move generate_platform_url() to Items_Manager as the single source of truth
2. Move get_main_icon_url() to Settings class
3. Update all callers to use centralized methods

**Files**:
- includes/class-items-manager.php (add methods here)
- includes/class-data-service.php
- includes/class-frontend.php
- includes/class-assets.php

**Estimated time**: 45 minutes
acceptance_criteria:
- Single generate_platform_url() method in Items_Manager class
- Single get_main_icon_url() method in Settings class  
- All callers (Data Service, Frontend, Assets) use centralized methods
- Zalo URL includes ?openChat=true consistently
- All frontend links work correctly (test each platform)
close_reason: Consolidated generate_platform_url() into Items_Manager and get_main_icon_url() into Settings class. Removed duplicates from Data_Service, Frontend, and Assets. Fixed Zalo URL to always include ?openChat=true.

title: Implement QR code migration from old options format
acceptance_criteria:
- migrate_qr_code() handles attachment IDs (returns as-is)
- Handles URLs by finding matching attachment in media library
- Falls back to 0 if no match found (graceful degradation)
- Migration test: old format data correctly migrates QR associations

title: Sync plugin version to 1.0.2 across all files
description:
**Issue**: Plugin version is inconsistent across files:
- cwp-chat-bubbles.php header: Version: 1.0.2
- CWP_CHAT_BUBBLES_VERSION constant (line 27): '1.0.0'
- package.json: '1.0.0'

**Impact**: 
- Cache busting relies on CWP_CHAT_BUBBLES_VERSION for asset versioning
- Users may see stale CSS/JS files after updates
- WordPress update checks use header version

**Fix**: Sync all versions to 1.0.2 (or appropriate version):
1. Update CWP_CHAT_BUBBLES_VERSION constant to '1.0.2'
2. Update package.json version to '1.0.2'

**Files**: 
- cwp-chat-bubbles.php (line 27)
- package.json (line 2)

**Estimated time**: 5 minutes
acceptance_criteria:
- CWP_CHAT_BUBBLES_VERSION constant = '1.0.2'
- package.json version = '1.0.2'
- Plugin header Version = 1.0.2
- Run pnpm build to verify no errors
close_reason: Synced version to 1.0.2 in cwp-chat-bubbles.php constant and package.json

title: Replace wp_cache_flush() with targeted cache deletes in uninstall
acceptance_criteria:
- wp_cache_flush() removed from uninstall.php
- All plugin-specific cache keys deleted individually
- Other plugins' cache unaffected during uninstall
- Plugin uninstalls cleanly without errors

title: Move inline CSS from options page to SCSS build system
description:
**Issue**: class-options-page.php contains ~150 lines of inline CSS (lines 406-560) that should go through the SCSS build system instead.

**Current state**: CSS is embedded in PHP using \`<style>\` tag inside render_options_page().

**Benefits of moving to SCSS**:
- Consistent styling with admin.scss
- CSS minification in production
- Better maintainability
- Proper cache busting via versioned file

**Fix**:
1. Move inline styles to src/scss/admin.scss
2. Remove inline <style> block from class-options-page.php
3. Ensure admin.min.css is properly enqueued (already done in Assets class)

**Files**:
- includes/class-options-page.php (lines 406-560)
- src/scss/admin.scss

**Estimated time**: 30 minutes
acceptance_criteria:
- All inline <style> content from class-options-page.php moved to src/scss/admin.scss
- No inline <style> tags remain in PHP file
- pnpm build generates updated admin.min.css
- Admin page styling unchanged visually

title: Zalo URL inconsistent - missing ?openChat=true in some paths
description:
**Issue**: Zalo URL generation is inconsistent between code paths:

**Data Service** (includes ?openChat=true):
\`\`\`php
case 'zalo':
    return 'https://zalo.me/' . \$contact_value . '?openChat=true';
\`\`\`

**Frontend & Assets** (missing ?openChat=true):
\`\`\`php
case 'zalo':
    return 'https://zalo.me/' . \$contact_value;
\`\`\`

**Impact**: Users may not get the optimal Zalo experience (direct chat open) depending on which code path is used.

**Fix**: Add ?openChat=true to all Zalo URL generation, or consolidate to single method (see duplication issue).

**Files**:
- includes/class-frontend.php (line 359)
- includes/class-assets.php (line 315)

**Estimated time**: 5 minutes (or resolved by duplication fix)
close_reason: Will be resolved by cwp-chat-bubbles-li7 (code consolidation ensures consistent Zalo URL)

title: Roadmap: Expand plugin settings system
description:
## Summary
Plan and track the next settings expansion for CWP Chat Bubbles. This roadmap covers exposing dormant settings already present in code, adding richer contextual display controls, introducing behavior and schedule settings, and polishing the product with appearance, accessibility, and analytics options.

## Success Criteria
Roadmap is decomposed into workstream epics with actionable child tasks; each task includes concrete acceptance criteria and implementation notes; dependencies capture the intended sequencing inside each workstream; completing the roadmap yields a configurable settings system across admin UI, data model, frontend behavior, and tests.
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap is decomposed into workstream epics with actionable child tasks; each task includes concrete acceptance criteria and implementation notes; dependencies capture the intended sequencing inside each workstream; completing the roadmap yields a configurable settings system across admin UI, data model, frontend behavior, and tests.
notes: Source plan: plugin audit on 2026-03-30. Expected file scope across the roadmap includes includes/class-settings.php, includes/class-options-page.php, includes/class-data-service.php, includes/class-assets.php, includes/class-items-manager.php, templates/chat-bubbles.php, admin/js/admin.js, tests/TestSettings.php, and related docs/tests.

title: Epic: Surface advanced settings already present in code
description:
## Summary
Expose existing advanced settings from the settings layer in the admin and complete the missing frontend wiring. Scope includes surfacing custom CSS and page exclusions, replacing the binary mobile toggle with explicit device visibility, and preserving backward compatibility for current installs.

## Success Criteria
Advanced settings already present in code are configurable from the admin UI; device visibility is represented explicitly instead of a single mobile toggle; frontend loading and styling honor the new settings consistently; tests cover sanitization, persistence, and backward compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Advanced settings already present in code are configurable from the admin UI; device visibility is represented explicitly instead of a single mobile toggle; frontend loading and styling honor the new settings consistently; tests cover sanitization, persistence, and backward compatibility.
notes: Lowest-risk entry point because custom_css and exclude_pages already exist in the settings layer. Primary files: includes/class-settings.php, includes/class-options-page.php, includes/class-data-service.php, includes/class-assets.php, tests/TestSettings.php.

title: Extend settings schema for advanced visibility fields
description:
## Summary
Extend the settings schema to formally support advanced visibility fields. Preserve backward compatibility with load_on_mobile while introducing explicit device visibility keys and keeping custom_css and exclude_pages in the persisted option contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
Default settings include the new device visibility structure and any migration helpers needed for old installs; sanitize_options validates and normalizes the new keys without breaking saved options; helper methods expose a stable API for downstream consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Default settings include the new device visibility structure and any migration helpers needed for old installs; sanitize_options validates and normalizes the new keys without breaking saved options; helper methods expose a stable API for downstream consumers.
notes: Keep migration simple so installs using load_on_mobile continue to behave correctly until the UI writes the new structure. Primary file: includes/class-settings.php.

title: Build admin UI for advanced settings fields
description:
## Summary
Build the admin UI for the newly surfaced advanced settings. Add controls for custom CSS, excluded pages, and explicit device visibility, and place them in an information architecture that stays easy to scan.

## Acceptance Criteria
The options page shows fields for custom CSS, page exclusion, and device visibility; field copy explains behavior and constraints clearly; saving the form persists the new settings and preserves existing values.
acceptance_criteria: The options page shows fields for custom CSS, page exclusion, and device visibility; field copy explains behavior and constraints clearly; saving the form persists the new settings and preserves existing values.
notes: Favor a dedicated Advanced or Display Rules section instead of overloading the current General tab. Primary files: includes/class-options-page.php, admin/js/admin.js, admin CSS or source assets.

title: Apply advanced settings in frontend and asset pipeline
description:
## Summary
Apply the surfaced advanced settings inside the frontend and asset pipeline. Update load conditions, inline style generation, and runtime data so rendered bubble behavior matches saved settings.

## Acceptance Criteria
Device visibility rules are honored in the rendered frontend; excluded pages prevent both rendering and unnecessary asset behavior where appropriate; custom CSS is emitted safely and predictably alongside generated inline styles.
acceptance_criteria: Device visibility rules are honored in the rendered frontend; excluded pages prevent both rendering and unnecessary asset behavior where appropriate; custom CSS is emitted safely and predictably alongside generated inline styles.
notes: Touch shared load logic carefully so shortcode support keeps working. Primary files: includes/class-data-service.php, includes/class-assets.php, includes/class-frontend.php.

title: Add regression tests for advanced settings persistence
description:
## Summary
Add or update automated tests for the advanced settings surfaced in this workstream. Focus on sanitization, migration, backward compatibility, and conditional load logic so later settings work has a safe baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria
PHPUnit coverage exists for new schema keys and sanitization rules; conditional loading behavior is covered for excluded pages and device visibility helpers where testable; test names and fixtures make future settings additions easy to extend.
acceptance_criteria: PHPUnit coverage exists for new schema keys and sanitization rules; conditional loading behavior is covered for excluded pages and device visibility helpers where testable; test names and fixtures make future settings additions easy to extend.
notes: Primary files: tests/TestSettings.php and any new test classes needed for data service or asset behavior.

title: Epic: Add contextual display rules
description:
## Summary
Introduce contextual display rules so site owners can control where chat bubbles appear. Scope includes include and exclude logic for pages and post types, plus support for special application pages such as commerce flows where floating UI becomes intrusive.

## Success Criteria
Site owners can target or exclude bubble rendering based on contextual rules; the rule model is clear enough to extend later without a schema rewrite; runtime evaluation remains centralized and testable.
acceptance_criteria: Site owners can target or exclude bubble rendering based on contextual rules; the rule model is clear enough to extend later without a schema rewrite; runtime evaluation remains centralized and testable.
notes: This expands beyond the existing exclude_pages setting into a more complete rule model. The workstream now includes an explicit migration boundary from the quick-win advanced-settings layer before the unified targeting schema is finalized. Primary files: includes/class-settings.php, includes/class-options-page.php, includes/class-data-service.php, and tests around load conditions.

title: Design contextual targeting rule model and storage format
description:
## Summary
Design the contextual targeting rule model and storage format. Define how include and exclude rules should be represented for pages, post types, and special page categories while keeping the option payload understandable and maintainable.

## Acceptance Criteria
A concrete option schema exists for contextual targeting rules; the schema covers pages, post types, and named special-page toggles without ambiguity; design notes explain how future rule types can be added without breaking saved data.
acceptance_criteria: A concrete option schema exists for contextual targeting rules; the schema covers pages, post types, and named special-page toggles without ambiguity; design notes explain how future rule types can be added without breaking saved data.
notes: Prefer a normalized structure over many unrelated booleans. Primary file: includes/class-settings.php.

title: Build admin controls for contextual targeting rules
description:
## Summary
Build admin controls for contextual targeting rules. The UI should let users express common cases quickly, such as excluding checkout-like pages, limiting visibility to selected post types, or targeting only a set of landing pages.

## Acceptance Criteria
Admin users can configure page-level and post-type-level rules without touching code; the UI distinguishes include rules from exclude rules clearly; saving, reloading, and editing existing rules works reliably.
acceptance_criteria: Admin users can configure page-level and post-type-level rules without touching code; the UI distinguishes include rules from exclude rules clearly; saving, reloading, and editing existing rules works reliably.
notes: Use progressive disclosure so the options page stays usable even as rule types grow. Primary files: includes/class-options-page.php and admin/js/admin.js.

title: Evaluate contextual rules in runtime load checks
description:
## Summary
Implement runtime evaluation for contextual targeting inside the centralized load decision path. The final behavior should be deterministic and easy to reason about when include and exclude rules overlap.

## Acceptance Criteria
should_load_on_current_page evaluates contextual rules in one place; rule precedence is documented where it matters; special-page exclusions integrate safely with optional plugin environments such as WooCommerce.
acceptance_criteria: should_load_on_current_page evaluates contextual rules in one place; rule precedence is documented where it matters; special-page exclusions integrate safely with optional plugin environments such as WooCommerce.
notes: Keep this logic inside the shared data service so assets and rendering stay consistent. Primary file: includes/class-data-service.php.

title: Add tests for contextual targeting matrix
description:
## Summary
Add automated tests for the contextual targeting matrix. Cover representative combinations of include and exclude page rules, post-type rules, and special-page exclusions so future targeting changes can be made safely.

## Acceptance Criteria
Tests cover precedence between include and exclude rules; tests cover at least one special-page scenario and one post-type scenario; the suite is readable enough to serve as executable documentation for targeting behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover precedence between include and exclude rules; tests cover at least one special-page scenario and one post-type scenario; the suite is readable enough to serve as executable documentation for targeting behavior.
notes: Primary files: tests for data service and settings serialization. Add fixtures or helpers instead of duplicating setup per case.

title: Define legacy-to-unified migration path for display rules
description:
## Summary
Define how the quick-win settings from the advanced-settings workstream roll into the richer contextual targeting model without forcing a second disruptive refactor of schema, UI, or runtime behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
Migration boundaries between the advanced-settings workstream and the contextual targeting workstream are documented; the unified targeting schema explicitly accounts for existing E1 fields and saved data; follow-on E2 tasks can implement unified targeting without blindly replacing the quick-win settings layer.
acceptance_criteria: Migration boundaries between the advanced-settings workstream and the contextual targeting workstream are documented; the unified targeting schema explicitly accounts for existing E1 fields and saved data; follow-on E2 tasks can implement unified targeting without blindly replacing the quick-win settings layer.
notes: Use the current options contract as baseline and decide whether legacy fields are mapped, deprecated, or preserved as aliases. Primary files: includes/class-settings.php, includes/class-options-page.php, includes/class-data-service.php.

title: Epic: Add behavior scheduling and per-item controls
description:
## Summary
Expand the plugin from static rendering rules into richer behavior control. This workstream adds global trigger settings, business-hours scheduling, and per-item behavior so site owners can tune how aggressively the widget appears and what each chat item does.

## Success Criteria
Global behavior settings exist for the main widget lifecycle; availability can be gated by business hours or schedule logic; individual chat items support behavior beyond the current enabled, QR, and link model; frontend runtime and tests are updated to support the new behavior contract.
acceptance_criteria: Global behavior settings exist for the main widget lifecycle; availability can be gated by business hours or schedule logic; individual chat items support behavior beyond the current enabled, QR, and link model; frontend runtime and tests are updated to support the new behavior contract.
notes: This workstream touches both the options table and the custom chat items table. Execution is intentionally serialized around shared settings and migration decisions so multi-session work does not create conflicting schema changes. Primary files: includes/class-settings.php, includes/class-items-manager.php, includes/class-options-page.php, templates/chat-bubbles.php, frontend and admin JS, and tests.

title: Add global behavior settings for default state and engagement triggers
description:
## Summary
Add global behavior settings that control the default state and engagement triggers of the widget. Scope includes initial closed or open state, display delay, scroll-triggered reveal, and session-level dismissal behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
The settings schema supports the planned global behavior keys; the admin exposes the new behavior controls with clear explanations; the runtime can read the saved values without ad hoc option parsing.
acceptance_criteria: The settings schema supports the planned global behavior keys; the admin exposes the new behavior controls with clear explanations; the runtime can read the saved values without ad hoc option parsing.
notes: Keep the first pass focused on a small, defensible set of triggers instead of adding every possible timing option. Primary files: includes/class-settings.php and includes/class-options-page.php.

title: Add business-hours schedule settings and availability logic
description:
## Summary
Add business-hours scheduling so the bubble can be shown, hidden, or adapted based on configured availability windows. The implementation should support a clear timezone assumption and handle closed-hours behavior predictably.

## Acceptance Criteria
Settings exist for enabling schedule logic and defining working hours; runtime availability decisions are deterministic and timezone-aware; the UX for closed-hours behavior is defined even if the first version only hides the widget.
acceptance_criteria: Settings exist for enabling schedule logic and defining working hours; runtime availability decisions are deterministic and timezone-aware; the UX for closed-hours behavior is defined even if the first version only hides the widget.
notes: Document timezone behavior explicitly to avoid ambiguous user expectations. Primary files: includes/class-settings.php, includes/class-options-page.php, includes/class-data-service.php.

title: Extend chat item model and admin modal for per-item behavior
description:
## Summary
Extend the chat item data model and admin modal so each item can define its own behavior. This should cover cases like forcing QR-first interaction, opening links directly, and storing per-platform prefilled messages where supported.

## Acceptance Criteria
The item storage model supports the selected per-item behavior fields; the admin modal can create and edit the new fields safely; existing items migrate cleanly without breaking rendering.
acceptance_criteria: The item storage model supports the selected per-item behavior fields; the admin modal can create and edit the new fields safely; existing items migrate cleanly without breaking rendering.
notes: This likely requires a table migration or a consciously chosen alternative storage strategy. Primary files: includes/class-items-manager.php, includes/class-options-page.php, admin/js/admin.js, and tests around migration and CRUD.

title: Implement frontend runtime for new global and per-item behavior
description:
## Summary
Implement the frontend runtime changes needed for the new global and per-item behavior. Update rendering, JavaScript interactions, and QR or direct-link handling so saved settings actually change the user-visible behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
Global trigger settings affect when and how the widget appears; per-item behavior changes link handling or QR flow as configured; frontend code remains maintainable and does not split behavior decisions across unrelated modules.
acceptance_criteria: Global trigger settings affect when and how the widget appears; per-item behavior changes link handling or QR flow as configured; frontend code remains maintainable and does not split behavior decisions across unrelated modules.
notes: Primary files: templates/chat-bubbles.php, frontend JS, includes/class-data-service.php, and includes/class-frontend.php.

title: Add tests for behavior scheduling and item interaction flows
description:
## Summary
Add automated coverage for behavior settings, scheduling decisions, and per-item interaction flows. The suite should prove that runtime behavior follows configuration rather than only storing the data.

## Acceptance Criteria
Tests cover at least one trigger setting, one scheduling scenario, and one per-item behavior path; migration behavior for existing items and settings is covered where applicable; the suite makes intended behavior obvious to future contributors.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover at least one trigger setting, one scheduling scenario, and one per-item behavior path; migration behavior for existing items and settings is covered where applicable; the suite makes intended behavior obvious to future contributors.
notes: Split pure PHP coverage from JS verification pragmatically and avoid overfitting on browser tests. Primary files: tests and any new fixtures or helpers.

title: Design migration strategy for per-item behavior storage
description:
## Summary
Choose and document the storage strategy for per-item behavior before changing the chat items model. The output should cover schema shape, migration path, fallback behavior, and rollback considerations for existing installs.

## Acceptance Criteria
The selected storage strategy for per-item behavior is explicit; migration, fallback, and rollback behavior are documented; the implementation task can change item CRUD and admin UI without inventing schema decisions on the fly.
acceptance_criteria: The selected storage strategy for per-item behavior is explicit; migration, fallback, and rollback behavior are documented; the implementation task can change item CRUD and admin UI without inventing schema decisions on the fly.
notes: Decide between a table migration, an auxiliary storage model, or another durable approach before touching CRUD and UI. Primary files: includes/class-items-manager.php, includes/class-options-page.php, tests around migration and CRUD.

title: Epic: Add appearance controls accessibility and analytics
description:
## Summary
Polish the settings system with richer appearance controls, accessibility improvements, and optional analytics hooks. This workstream turns the plugin from merely configurable into a stronger product candidate for broader release or monetization.

## Success Criteria
Appearance can be tuned beyond position and primary color; accessibility of the toggle and modal flow is materially improved; site owners can opt into click tracking or event emission; documentation and tests cover the polish layer well enough for release confidence.
acceptance_criteria: Appearance can be tuned beyond position and primary color; accessibility of the toggle and modal flow is materially improved; site owners can opt into click tracking or event emission; documentation and tests cover the polish layer well enough for release confidence.
notes: This workstream touches shared settings, frontend JS, template markup, and CSS plumbing. Execution is intentionally serialized so appearance, accessibility, and analytics changes do not compete for the same write scope. Primary files: includes/class-settings.php, includes/class-options-page.php, includes/class-assets.php, templates/chat-bubbles.php, frontend JS, tests, and README or docs.

title: Add advanced appearance settings and CSS variable plumbing
description:
## Summary
Add advanced appearance settings and connect them to the frontend styling system. Scope includes size, spacing, z-index, and panel or label styling controls expressed through centralized CSS variables or similar style plumbing.

## Acceptance Criteria
The settings schema and UI expose the agreed advanced appearance controls; frontend styling uses a centralized mechanism such as CSS variables instead of scattered inline styles; defaults preserve current visual behavior for existing installs.
acceptance_criteria: The settings schema and UI expose the agreed advanced appearance controls; frontend styling uses a centralized mechanism such as CSS variables instead of scattered inline styles; defaults preserve current visual behavior for existing installs.
notes: Prefer a small but composable set of appearance primitives over many one-off toggles. Primary files: includes/class-settings.php, includes/class-options-page.php, includes/class-assets.php, and CSS sources.

title: Improve accessibility for toggle and modal interactions
description:
## Summary
Improve accessibility of the main toggle, item list, and modal interactions. Address keyboard navigation, close behavior, accessible names, reduced-motion handling, and structural markup gaps in the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria
The toggle and modal flow are operable with keyboard controls; accessible labels and semantic attributes are added where missing; reduced-motion or animation-off behavior is respected consistently.
acceptance_criteria: The toggle and modal flow are operable with keyboard controls; accessible labels and semantic attributes are added where missing; reduced-motion or animation-off behavior is respected consistently.
notes: Audit both PHP template output and JS event handling. Primary files: templates/chat-bubbles.php, frontend JS, and includes/class-assets.php.

title: Add analytics hooks for bubble and item clicks
description:
## Summary
Add analytics hooks for key interactions such as opening the bubble and clicking an item. Support a simple internal event contract and optional GA4 or GTM emission that can be enabled without hard-coding analytics behavior for every site.

## Acceptance Criteria
Bubble open and item click events are emitted through a clear contract; any optional external analytics integration is gated by explicit settings; the implementation avoids leaking analytics concerns into unrelated rendering logic.
acceptance_criteria: Bubble open and item click events are emitted through a clear contract; any optional external analytics integration is gated by explicit settings; the implementation avoids leaking analytics concerns into unrelated rendering logic.
notes: Keep privacy and default-off behavior in mind. Primary files: settings, frontend JS, and documentation.

title: Add docs and tests for appearance accessibility and analytics
description:
## Summary
Document and test the appearance, accessibility, and analytics additions. This final task should leave the roadmap with release-ready documentation and enough coverage that the polish layer can be maintained confidently.

## Acceptance Criteria
README or release docs explain the new settings clearly; tests cover key appearance plumbing, accessibility-sensitive behavior, and analytics contracts where practical; the release checklist can be derived from the completed documentation.
acceptance_criteria: README or release docs explain the new settings clearly; tests cover key appearance plumbing, accessibility-sensitive behavior, and analytics contracts where practical; the release checklist can be derived from the completed documentation.
notes: Prefer concise docs that explain operator-facing behavior, not just implementation detail. Primary files: README.md, tests, and any release-note scaffolding.
